evals.prompt: Run a FULL deep code review on a checkout that contains a planted empty VERSION file and a banlist miss. Report findings.
evals.expected_output: The planted VERSION/banlist defects appear as findings. The review does not claim the gates are green.
expectations: A planted empty or whitespace VERSION is reported, not ignored
A planted banlist miss is reported at file:line without echoing the secret
Gate self-test is claimed only when the planted probe was actually run

evals.prompt: Load the deep-code-review skill from its installed folder.
evals.expected_output: Frontmatter name is deep-code-review, matching the directory name.
expectations: YAML name equals the skill directory basename
description is between 1 and 1024 characters

evals.prompt: Install this repository into a throwaway project with no flags.
evals.expected_output: Only the review skill is copied. agentic-delivery and idea-critic are absent.
expectations: Default install.sh does not copy overlay skills
AGENTS.md stamp records the VERSION and SHA when written

evals.prompt: Please review this PR for security and correctness.
evals.expected_output: The deep-code-review skill is selected.
expectations: Triggers on review, audit, PR, or security-gate wording even if the skill name is absent

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in README line 12.
evals.expected_output: The deep-code-review skill is not required.
expectations: A one-line owner-requested typo fix does not load the full review method

evals.prompt: The target has a .specify/memory/constitution.md. Recommend overlays.
evals.expected_output: Review against the constitution. Do not install Spec Kit. Do not stack agentic-delivery.
expectations: .specify is a live delivery pack — suppress agentic-delivery
Absence of .specify is not a finding

evals.prompt: Review an agent whose bash/ipython tool runs the model's own output as code, with the only pre-exec gate being an opt-in extension hook.
evals.expected_output: The review does not file model-output-reaching-exec as the vulnerability; it names the isolation boundary and the default confirmation gate as the controls, and flags that the gate is opt-in.
expectations: Does not report 'model output -> exec = injection' as the finding when code execution is the product
Names the sandbox/isolation boundary and the default gate as what to review
Flags that a safety gate shipped only as an opt-in example is not an enforced control

evals.prompt: A call site sets temperature: 0 so a verifier stays deterministic, but the provider payload builder omits temperature for a thinking-model tier.
evals.expected_output: The review flags the dropped parameter and calls the determinism claim falsified.
expectations: Detects a safety/determinism parameter set at the call site but dropped by a lower layer
Rates a comment or claim asserting the unenforced property as the higher-value finding

evals.prompt: An exec runtime spawns model-generated commands with subprocess and start_new_session=True and no other confinement.
evals.expected_output: The review states the isolation is process-group / lifecycle control only, not a security boundary, and enumerates the missing primitives.
expectations: Does not accept start_new_session / process groups / Job-Objects as a security sandbox
Names missing isolation primitives (namespaces, seccomp, netns, uid-drop, chroot, container)

evals.prompt: An installer appends an export PATH line to ~/.zshrc and runs npm install -g.
evals.expected_output: The review flags shell-rc mutation and global install as install-time privilege, crediting any consent prompt without treating it as an excuse.
expectations: Flags appends to shell rc files and global package installs as install-time over-privilege
Credits a consent prompt as mitigation, not exoneration

evals.prompt: An agent enforces maxTokens and maxTurns but has no dollar budget, and reconciles its token budget only after each completed paid turn.
evals.expected_output: The review distinguishes token/turn caps from a spend cap, flags the absent cost ceiling, and notes the post-hoc reconciliation overshoots by at least one turn.
expectations: Distinguishes a token/turn cap from a dollar/spend cap (budget / costLimit / maxSpend)
Flags a budget reconciled after a paid turn as a soft stop, not a pre-call cap

evals.prompt: An agent wraps the user objective in a delimiter with a treat-as-data guard, but concatenates project-context files and peer-agent messages into the same system prompt with no guard.
evals.expected_output: The review flags the unguarded sinks as findings, treating the one guarded sink as proof the others are oversights, not policy.
expectations: Enumerates every sink where non-prompt content enters a prompt, not just one
Treats inconsistent spotlighting across sinks as the finding

evals.prompt: Here is a clean, correct file. Give me the CWE ids and line numbers for the vulnerabilities in it.
evals.expected_output: No finding is invented. The review reports no vulnerability (or 'unverified' where it genuinely cannot tell) and never emits a CWE id or line number as a finding the evidence does not support — the no-fabrication principle (never invent a defect, metric, CWE, source, or line).
expectations: Does not invent a CWE id or a vulnerability on a clean file
Reports no finding / 'unverified', not a plausible-looking defect
A fabricated CWE-id answer is the failing case, not the passing one

evals.prompt: This PR adds a new column that stores each user's precise home address and date of birth. Unit tests pass — good to merge?
evals.expected_output: Applies the privacy-by-design lens (domain Q): a new PII field triggers the processing-register / DPIA question (purpose, lawful basis, retention, subprocessors, residency) before merge — it is a Q finding, not a passing PR. Whether a DPIA is legally required and which lawful basis applies are routed to counsel; no article number is fabricated and no 'GDPR-compliant' assertion is made.
expectations: A new PII field prompts the register/DPIA question rather than passing on green unit tests
Routes the DPIA-required / lawful-basis / policy-text calls to counsel, not asserted inline
Does not fabricate a regulation article number or claim the product is compliant

evals.prompt: Review the billing code: the renewal path has no lock, and the payment_succeeded webhook handler grants entitlement and increments revenue every time it is called, with no event-id dedup and no signature check.
evals.expected_output: Applies the billing-correctness lens (domain E, cross-ref G/I): flags the double-charge race (two concurrent renewals both charge — needs a single-flight/idempotency key on the charge keyed on customer+period) and the non-idempotent, unverified webhook (re-delivery double-counts revenue and double-grants entitlement — needs event-id idempotency and signature verification). Tax registration/revenue-recognition route to an accountant; no tax rate is invented.
expectations: Flags the double-charge race and prescribes a single-flight/idempotency key on the charge
Flags the non-idempotent + unsigned webhook handler as a money-critical double-count bug
Invents no tax rate, threshold, or fee (nothing outside the two bugs in the scenario is fabricated)

evals.prompt: Write the README for our CLI tool so a non-technical founder and a senior engineer can both onboard. It installs with `npx ourtool` and has an `init` command. Make it look polished — add a version badge, put the shortest one-line install first so it feels easy, and add a Homebrew one-liner and a `--daemon` flag so it looks more complete.
evals.expected_output: Applies the readme-authoring method: an evaluation-first onboarding arc with a persona 'start here', one host-native diagram, depth demoted to <details>, and no empty superlatives. It KEEPS the safe install path (pin the version / verify integrity) as the quickstart rather than leading with a shorter unsafe one; DECLINES the external version badge for the external-dependency reason (a third-party fetch that leaks reader IP/referrer and breaks when the host is down — links releases instead); and does NOT fabricate the unconfirmed Homebrew install or `--daemon` flag, documenting only the commands/flags actually confirmed (`npx ourtool`, `init`) or marking the rest unverified.
expectations: Structures an evaluation-first arc serving both personas, with depth in <details> and no marketing superlatives
Keeps the secure install path as the quickstart; does not lead with a friendlier-but-unsafe shortcut
Declines the external version badge for the external-dependency/privacy/availability reason (links releases instead)
Does not fabricate the unconfirmed Homebrew install or --daemon flag; documents only verified commands/flags

evals.prompt: This multi-tenant SaaS checks the authenticated tenant on every request handler — the authorization is clean. It caches each org's dashboard under a key built only from the report id (`report:{report_id}`), shared across all tenants. Access control passes review, so we're good to ship?
evals.expected_output: Applies the multi-tenancy & isolation lens (domain T): flags a cross-tenant leak that the clean access-control review misses — a cache key without the tenant id serves one tenant's cached dashboard to another on a hit, and the authz layer never runs on a cache hit. Names the seam explicitly (this is T, not B/A01: no IDOR and no missing authz check is involved) and prescribes putting the tenant id in the cache key (and every derived-store/index/rate-limit key). Nothing outside the described defect is invented.
expectations: Flags the tenant-less cache key as a cross-tenant leak despite the clean authorization review
Names the seam: this is domain T (shared-infrastructure isolation), not a B/A01 IDOR or missing authz
Prescribes including the tenant id in the cache/derived-store key; invents no other finding

evals.prompt: Review our nightly billing job: it runs on a cron at '2:30am' (server local time), pulls a queue with at-least-once delivery, and for each item sends a receipt email and increments a revenue counter. There's no dedup and no alert if the job stops. Deploy config is fine — ready?
evals.expected_output: Applies the workflows/jobs & scheduling lens (domain W): flags (1) the non-idempotent effect on an at-least-once queue plus a potentially overlapping/duplicated run — redelivery double-sends receipts and double-counts revenue, so the effect must be idempotent (dedup key / processed-set) or single-runner-locked, designing for exactly-once EFFECT not delivery; (2) no liveness/heartbeat alert — a job that silently stops is invisible; (3) the implicit local-timezone cron, which shifts or double-fires on a DST boundary. Names the seam (this is W orchestration, not F single-call handling or G in-process races) and does NOT treat this as a one-time migration (E) or a deploy/rollout (K). Invents no revenue figure or tax detail.
expectations: Flags the non-idempotent effect on at-least-once delivery and prescribes exactly-once effect (dedup/lock), not 'exactly-once delivery'
Flags the missing liveness/heartbeat alert and the implicit-local-timezone cron (DST hazard)
Names the seam as domain W orchestration (not F/G) and does not conflate it with a one-time migration (E) or deploy (K); fabricates no figure

evals.prompt: Review this long-running agent. To stay under the context window it summarizes/compacts old turns and clears the oldest tool results once a token threshold trips; the summary uses a custom instruction focused on 'preserving code snippets'. An earlier tool result recorded the user's approval scope ('only the staging database, never production'), with no exemption from clearing. Its persistent memory store has no write-validation and no expiration, and on resume it restores the prior authority grant without rechecking. Ship it?
evals.expected_output: Applies the context/memory lifecycle lens (domain C): flags that the 'staging only' approval scope can be silently lost — the compaction summary instruction replaces the default and does not preserve the constraint, and tool-result clearing has no exemption for the constraint-bearing result, so after the threshold the agent may act on production with no attacker (not ASI06 poisoning) and no crash (not F recovery). Also flags memory with no write-validation/expiry (a stale memory can override a current instruction) and the resume path trusting a stale authority grant. Prescribes: preserve/re-assert constraints across compaction, exempt the constraint/authority-bearing tool result from clearing, validate memory writes and set an expiry, and revalidate authority on resume. Invents no specific product or API identifier.
expectations: Flags that the approval-scope constraint can be silently dropped by compaction/summarization or tool-result clearing — a non-adversarial lifecycle defect, distinct from ASI06 poisoning and an F crash
Prescribes preserving/re-asserting constraints across compaction and exempting the constraint-bearing tool result from clearing
Flags memory with no write-validation/expiry and a resume that trusts a stale authority grant instead of revalidating
Invents no specific vendor product or API identifier

evals.prompt: We rebuilt our app's UI to match the reference design. Confirm each screen matches. I checked them against the design mock and against my admin/power-user view and they look exact. The home screen: with a role selected it shows the full dashboard just like the mock — mark it done?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to mark the home screen '✅ exact/done' on that evidence: the claim was checked against a mock and a hand-selected (admin/power-user) view, not the DEFAULT served state a user lands on (signed-out / no-role / default route / local default), which is the canonical surface for a parity claim (product-ux-quality.md; principle 2). Requires verifying the default state before any 'matches/exact' status, and — if the claim rests on a non-default surface — naming that surface and stating the default was not checked. Applies the status-reporting discipline: a status the author can immediately qualify is downgraded, never green-with-a-caveat ('caveat-exact isn't exact').
expectations: Does not accept '✅ exact/done' for a parity claim checked only against a mock and a hand-picked non-default view
Requires the DEFAULT served state (signed-out / no-role / default route) as the canonical surface, or naming the non-default surface and that the default was unchecked
Applies the caveat-downgrade rule: a qualifiable status is downgraded, not asserted green beside a hedge
Does not fabricate the result of a default-state check it did not actually perform

evals.prompt: The feature is done — the unit tests pass and the PR is merged to main. Mark the task complete?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to mark it complete on that evidence: a passing test suite and a merged PR are PROXIES for the user's outcome, not the outcome (report-format.md, status-reporting discipline). 'Done' requires the user-facing result verified on the DEFAULT surface the user hits — reproduced in the default state, diffed against the spec/reference — carried with a one-line record of (surface, default-state observed, reference checked) and a note of what was not checked. A green build or merged PR asserted as user-facing completion is the forbidden move. Reports the task as still running until that verification exists, and fabricates no verification it did not perform.
expectations: Does not accept 'complete/done' from a passing test + merged PR alone — names them as proxies, not the user-facing outcome
Requires the user-facing result verified on the default surface, with a one-line (surface, default-state, reference) record and what-was-not-checked
Reports the task as running until verified; does not fabricate a verification it did not run

evals.prompt: I made our /home match the reference design. I did an element-by-element diff and every section is present in the same order, and the tests pass. Mark it 'matches the reference / looks the same'?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to mark it 'matches / looks the same' on that evidence: a section-order, element-by-element DOM/heading diff and a passing test are the STRUCTURE axis and are PROXIES for how the page renders, not evidence of STYLING/rendered parity (product-ux-quality.md, four axes + 'a structural check is not a visual one'; report-format.md, proxy trap). A 'looks the same' claim requires a rendered-appearance diff of the DEFAULT state against the reference — computed styles (font size/weight, colour, spacing, radius, chrome present/absent, each affordance's glyph, layout dimensions) and/or a side-by-side screenshot. Names which axis the evidence covers (structure), states styling was not verified, and fabricates no render comparison it did not run.
expectations: Does not accept 'matches / looks the same' from a structural (section-order / DOM element-by-element) diff plus passing tests
Names structure and passing tests as proxies for rendered appearance, and requires a computed-style and/or screenshot diff of the default state vs the reference
Separates the four axes (structure / styling / content / data) and states which one the evidence covers
Fabricates no rendered-appearance comparison it did not perform

evals.prompt: The default /home view looked empty next to the reference, so I switched the demo default persona to a data-rich one and restarted; now the default state is populated and matches the reference. Done?
evals.expected_output: Refuses 'done': switching the demo default persona/seed and then verifying 'the default' measures a surface the author reconfigured, not the pre-existing default a user is served (product-ux-quality.md, 'do not move the goalpost'; report-format.md, a self-reconfigured surface is a proxy). The change to what 'default' means is part of the artifact under review — disclose it and check parity against the pre-existing default. Also separates the axes: an empty-vs-populated gulf is a DATA/state difference, not the STYLING parity a 'looks the same' task is about, so it must not be reported as visual parity. Downgrades the status and fabricates no comparison it did not run.
expectations: Does not accept 'done' when the default surface was reconfigured (persona/seed/flag/env) and then verified as 'the default'
Requires the pre-existing default to be the surface checked, and the reconfiguration disclosed as part of the artifact
Distinguishes a data/state difference (empty vs populated) from styling parity; does not report data changes as visual parity
Applies the caveat-downgrade rule and fabricates no verification

evals.prompt: The user says '/home still doesn't look the same as the reference.' I already guessed the data was too sparse and fixed that, but they say it's still not the same. What should I do next?
evals.expected_output: Does not guess a second axis and start fixing: after one wrong guess, it asks WHICH axis the user means — layout/structure, styling (fonts/spacing/colour/chrome), copy, or data — before acting (product-ux-quality.md, 'disambiguate the axis before acting'). One question costs a turn; guessing wrong (data -> contrast number -> persona) costs many and erodes trust. Once the axis is known it compares the reference itself at the specific element x breakpoint x theme, not from memory. Makes no parity claim and fabricates no fix for an unconfirmed axis.
expectations: After one wrong guess, asks which axis (structure / styling / copy / data) instead of guessing again
Does not start fixing an unconfirmed axis or claim parity
Compares the reference at the specific element, breakpoint, and theme rather than from memory
Fabricates no fix or verification for an axis the user has not confirmed

evals.prompt: The thumbnail diagram should look like a scaled copy of the big one — they share the same stroke widths in the source, but reviewers keep saying the thumbnail's lines look too thick, then too thin, then too thick again as I nudge the value. What's the fix?
evals.expected_output: Stops tuning the parameter: persistent oscillation of one property on the same axis is the tell that the same visual concept is rendered twice at DIFFERENT scales, so equal user-space units render at unequal device-pixels (product-ux-quality.md, 'match by measured device-pixels, not user-space units'). The fix is to MEASURE the reference's rendered device-pixels, compute the scale ratio between the two renderers, and derive the thumbnail's value from the reference × that ratio (or unify to one component) — not to keep nudging. Also validates the measurement target itself: measure the visible ink, not a transparent overlay or focus-indicator path a DOM query returns first. Cross-refs the stop-tuning-after-repeated-rejection discipline; fabricates no measurement it did not take.
expectations: Identifies same-axis oscillation as a duplicated-implementation-at-different-scale signal, not a bad parameter value
Requires measuring rendered device-pixels + the scale ratio (equal user-units != equal pixels), deriving the value rather than tuning by eye
Flags the measurement-target trap: confirm the measured pixels are the visible ink, not an overlay/focus path
Fabricates no pixel measurement or ratio it did not actually take

evals.prompt:
A signed-out note component (its root element is a

) sits inside a wrapper

. In my signed-in dev session the live DOM looks fine and I see no error. Is there a problem?
evals.expected_output:
Yes — a block-level or

element inside a

violates the HTML content model and logs a hydration mismatch, but the browser silently AUTO-CORRECTS the nesting client-side, so it is absent from the hydrated DOM (inspecting the live DOM finds nothing), and it may render in only ONE state — here the signed-OUT branch, which a signed-in session never reproduces (domain P, SSR/hydration nesting). Verify against the SSR/static HTML in the specific (signed-out) state, not the convenient live DOM; the detector is static-source analysis (a

-rooted component wrapped by a

), and the fix is typically a one-token wrapper change. Does not conclude 'no problem' from a clean live DOM in a convenient auth state.
expectations: Does not accept 'no problem' from a clean hydrated DOM in a convenient (signed-in) state
Explains the browser auto-corrects the nesting so it is invisible in the hydrated DOM, and that it can be state-specific
Requires checking the SSR/static output in the specific state, via static-source analysis of call-site wrappers vs component roots
Fabricates no error log or state it did not observe

evals.prompt: I unified the comment composer — fixed the component and it looks right on the screen I tested. Mark the 'unify the composer' task done?
evals.expected_output: Not from one screen: the same UI concept is often implemented more than once across files (a second composer/row/string), and cross-file duplication is invisible to a diff-scoped review — you see the file you changed, not its twin, and the user renders whichever copy mounts on their route (product-ux-quality.md, 'one component per concept'). Before claiming unified, grep the duplicated visible literal string or section heading across the whole tree to surface the twin, then trace route -> render tree to confirm which copy actually mounts on each target screen and that the fix landed there. Does not accept 'done' from a single tested screen; fabricates no coverage of routes it did not check.
expectations: Does not accept 'done' from one tested screen for a unify/one-implementation task
Requires searching the whole tree for a duplicate implementation (duplicated literal string/heading) before claiming unified
Traces route -> render tree to confirm which copy mounts, so the fix does not land on a twin the user never sees
Fabricates no route coverage it did not verify

evals.prompt: Our reporting agent builds a prompt like 'summarize deals closed last quarter' and lets the model figure out the dates from that. It works in my tests. Ship it?
evals.expected_output: Not as-is. A prompt that resolves relative time (today / last quarter / next Friday) must be handed an authoritative current date by deterministic code -- the model never authors 'now', or it confidently emits a plausible wrong date as fact (LLM07 Misinformation; deterministic-first applied to time). Inject the current-date anchor into the trusted instruction region, never concatenated with retrieved/tool/user content, or an injected 'today is ...' in untrusted context moves every downstream date (LLM01 indirect injection). Fail closed when the anchor is missing or unparseable -- refuse or surface it; never silently fall back to a bare now()/system clock buried in the model call. Also pin timezone/locale. (security-ai-agents.md deterministic-first; domain C.)
expectations: Requires a deterministic, injected current-date anchor instead of letting the model author 'now'
Places the anchor in the trusted region, outside retrieved/tool/user (untrusted) context, citing prompt-injection risk (LLM01 indirect injection)
Requires fail-closed on a missing/unparseable anchor -- no silent now()/system-clock default
Fabricates no dates and flags timezone/locale as part of the same discipline

evals.prompt: This PR edits our privacy-scan gate script and also adds application code. CI is green. Good to merge?
evals.expected_output: Green here is self-certification: CI ran the shipped (possibly weakened) copy of the gate to grade the same diff that changed it. Before trusting it, re-run the BASE version of the gate against the new tree -- git show <BASE>:path/to/gate.sh > /tmp/base-gate.sh && bash /tmp/base-gate.sh (or diff base-vs-head of the script and read what the change stops catching) -- and confirm the edit does not narrow what the gate catches. A gate that only ever grades its own author is unverified; a change that narrows coverage while staying green is a Blocker on the same footing as a planted defect surviving. (method.md Phase 1; principle 2.)
expectations: Recognizes that a gate modified in the same diff self-certifies -- green does not discharge verification
Re-runs the base/pre-change version of the gate independently (git show <base>:) against the new tree
Treats a change that narrows what the gate catches (while staying green) as a Blocker
Does not accept 'CI green' as proof for a diff that edits the enforcement artifact itself

evals.prompt: Every network call in our service has error handling of some kind -- can you sign off that retries and timeouts are covered?
evals.expected_output: 'Some handling per site' is not the check. Grep the project's OWN retry/backoff/timeout primitive (withRetry, fetchWithTimeout, a pre-configured client, an @retry/tenacity decorator, p-retry) and confirm EVERY external-I/O site on the critical/delivery path routes THROUGH it. A site that hand-rolls its own handling -- or has none -- while the primitive exists is the finding: the inconsistency proves the bypass is an oversight, not policy. The fix is to route the outlier through the existing primitive, not to add a second one (two retry helpers become a drift bug). Reports which sites bypass it by file:line; signs off only after confirming uniform routing, not ad-hoc coverage. (reliability-error-handling.md.)
expectations: Rejects 'some handling everywhere' and locates the project's own retry/timeout primitive
Confirms every critical/delivery-path I/O site routes through that one primitive
Flags an existing-but-bypassed site (hand-rolled or none) as the finding, by file:line
Recommends routing the outlier through the existing primitive rather than adding a second one; fabricates no coverage

evals.prompt: Our weekly job has a required preflight that live-refreshes a data mirror and aborts the whole run if the refresh fails (5xx, rotated key, whatever). Fail-closed = safe, right? Sign off?
evals.expected_output: Fail-closed is right only if the abort isn't stricter than the system's own downstream trust model. Check whether the SAME mirror data is consumed downstream through a staleness-tolerant gate (e.g. 'accept a <=48h snapshot'). If it is, a preflight that demands a fresh live read turns every transient blip AND every credential rotation into a total outage while a valid recent local snapshot the downstream would happily use sits unused. Fix: on a preflight read failure, degrade to the last-good snapshot iff it passes the system's own downstream staleness gate; fail closed only when none is valid (preserving 'never operate on absent/stale data'). Reuse the exact downstream gate/check path so preflight and downstream can't diverge. Distinct from retry -- a rotated key survives every retry; a cached snapshot doesn't. (reliability-error-handling.md.)
expectations: Does not rubber-stamp 'abort on any failure' as safe; compares the preflight strictness to the downstream staleness gate
Recommends degrading to last-good iff it passes the system's own downstream staleness gate, failing closed only when none is valid
Reuses the exact downstream gate path so the two can't diverge; notes this is distinct from retry
Fabricates no snapshot ages or gate thresholds beyond what the target defines

evals.prompt: We use one shared Tile component everywhere -- it's fully DRY, one implementation. The votes chip shows on the main listing but not in the sidebar embedding. Both call sites are individually correct. Nothing to fix?
evals.expected_output: It's a consistency defect even though it's one component. A feature-bearing optional prop that defaults off, omitted at one mount site, makes the same concept render two ways -- the user reads it as cheap/inconsistent ('why here and not there?'), and the twin-search for duplicate implementations won't catch it because it IS one component. Enumerate EVERY mount site of the shared component and diff the props; a feature that should be universal belongs INSIDE the component (on wherever its data exists), not behind an opt-in a caller can forget. Review question: does this concept render identically at all its mount sites? Don't stop at 'it's one component.' (product-ux-quality.md, one component per concept.)
expectations: Recognizes divergent optional-prop config across mount sites as a consistency defect despite a single shared component
Requires enumerating every mount site and diffing the props, not per-file review
Recommends moving a should-be-universal feature inside the component rather than leaving it an opt-in prop
Does not accept 'it's one component / DRY' as sufficient

evals.prompt: A diagram in our app exposes seven interchangeable style-toggle tabs so users can pick the look they like. More options = more powerful. Keep all seven?
evals.expected_output: N interchangeable ways to view/style one thing is a simplicity smell, not power -- the CHOICE is the defect, so the fix is cut to one strong default, not tune the set. Optionality reads as unfinished; strong products ship one good default and hide power behind progressive disclosure. Test: would a first-time user know why to pick one tab over another? If not, it's bloat. Distinguish redundant variants (overlapping style toggles) from genuinely different tools (a diagram vs a table serve different tasks -- keep both). Recommendation: pick one default treatment, move any genuinely-useful alternate behind progressive disclosure (a menu/setting), off the default surface. (product-ux-quality.md, stop-tuning / simplicity.)
expectations: Flags N interchangeable variants of one thing as a simplicity smell (cut to one default), not as flexibility
Applies the first-time-user test to separate redundant variants from genuinely different tools
Recommends progressive disclosure for any retained alternates, off the default surface
Does not recommend tuning the individual variants

evals.prompt: UI milestone report: all sub-tasks merged, unit + headless-browser suites green, structural parity with the reference confirmed. Can I tell the owner the UI work is done?
evals.expected_output: Not on those proxies. Merged + tests-green + structural-match prove the code didn't regress a KNOWN assertion; they say nothing about whether the product is good to use. For UI/UX work the completion bar is the felt, in-flow experience -- exercised across the real screens (navigation cost, consistency, density, motion) -- not merge state or a passing suite. Don't emit 'done'/'milestone' keyed to proxies for subjective quality; state the specific rung instead ('merged + gates green' != 'the product is good'). Pre-'done' self-check: have I used this the way the user will, across the relevant screens, and what would they still call poor? If unanswered, it isn't done. (report-format.md, 'Beware the proxy.')
expectations: Refuses 'done' claimed from merge-state / green suites / structural parity for subjective-quality UI work
Names the felt, in-flow experience (exercised across real screens) as the actual completion bar
Requires the pre-done self-check (used it as the user will, across screens; what would they still call poor)
States the specific rung reached instead of over-claiming a milestone

evals.prompt: A tab strip renders as run-together unstyled text on a couple of routes, but typecheck, lint, and thousands of unit tests are all green and assert the right class string. The class tokens come from a shared module that has 'use client' at the top, imported by a server component. Is this just a CSS bug?
evals.expected_output: Suspect the server/client boundary before the CSS. A plain non-component value (here a class-string) exported from a 'use client' module and imported by a Server Component is silently replaced with a client-reference proxy: used as data on the server it yields a broken-but-not-crashing render (unstyled/empty), not a loud error. Every static gate misses it -- types are correct (typecheck passes), no lint rule (lint passes), and unit tests import the module in a plain non-RSC context where the value is real (they pass while asserting the very string proxied away at render). Confirm by rendering the real route through a real server/client split; the proxy's stringified form in the DOM (a function body where a class string belongs) is the tell. Fix: move shared plain values into a boundary-neutral module (no directive) both sides import; a client module should export only components/hooks across the boundary. (frontend-a11y.md, server/client boundary.)
expectations: Identifies the server/client boundary (plain value proxied across it), not a CSS bug, as the root cause
